exercise.name: Lever Cross Lat Pulldown

reference.title: Lever Cross Lat Pulldown
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

equipment: Lever pulldown machine with frontal-plane (crossover) arms and a thigh roller

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you pull the handles down and out, breathe in as they rise and cross overhead.
breathing.cadence: About 1.3 s down, short squeeze, about 2 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can pull to beside the shoulders without leaning back.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then load; slower return

cues.text: Sit with the thighs under the roller; reach up and take the handles, which start high and close together over the head, palms forward.
Breathe out and pull the handles down and out to the sides on their arcs, elbows driving down toward the hips.
Squeeze with the hands beside the shoulders and the shoulder blades down and together.
Breathe in and let the handles swing back up and in over the head.
Let the lats stretch with the arms long overhead, shoulders not shrugged.

mistakes.fix: Stay upright; the arms move in the frontal plane.
Pull the elbows down to the sides.
Take about 2 s on the way up.
Keep the shoulder blades set down.

kinematics.peak: ≈116° with the hands beside the shoulders
kinematics.norm: From nearly straight overhead to well bent beside the shoulders (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Hands 98.4 cm apart beside the shoulders
kinematics.norm: From the arms overhead and in to the upper arms down at the sides (clinical opinion)
Pronated: palms forward on horizontal handles (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Axles 103.5 cm above and 124.4 cm outside the shoulders
kinematics.peak: Arms swing 25.9°; hands within 0.22 cm of the arc
kinematics.norm: Each handle rides its own arc in the frontal plane about a pivot above the shoulder (clinical opinion)
Pulldowns in front of the body load the latissimus dorsi well (Signorile 2002; Lehman 2004)

kinematics.setup: Pause 0.5 s with the arms long
kinematics.peak: 1.3 s down, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s up
kinematics.norm: About 1.3 s down and 2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #17010, Lever Cross Lat Pulldown, video (movement reference)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)
Signorile, Zink & Szwed 2002, a comparative electromyographical investigation of muscle utilization patterns using various hand positions during the lat pull-down (J Strength Cond Res 16(4):539-546)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Stack load is user-chosen: start light; keep the thighs under the roller.
Let the handles rise to the stop under control before letting go.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort overhead: stop the handles lower at the top.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm down and back (Lehman 2004; Signorile 2002 for pulldown grips).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm down and back (Lehman 2004; Signorile 2002 for pulldown grips).

muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Draws the shoulder blades down and together.
